title: Strengths interview
text: You tell us about concrete situations – what you did, not how you rate yourself. From that, strength themes can arise, each with the passage from your answer it rests on. You decide what fits you.

guidance.title: Before you start
guidance.time: Ten situations, three short counter-questions and one question about the outside view – about 30 to 40 minutes, feel free to do it in two sittings. You can finish after six answers.
guidance.stories: Describe one situation that actually happened each time – at work or in private life. What you did matters more than the outcome.
guidance.notCapability: This is not about fields of expertise or experience. What you bring professionally is covered by the capability interview.
guidance.save: Your answers are saved as you write. You can pause at any time.
guidance.private: Nobody but you sees your answers. They are only analyzed if you explicitly ask for it at the end.
guidance.noTest: This is not a test and not a typology. There are no points and no right answers.

progress.answered: {count, plural, =0 {no answer yet} one {one answer} other {# answers}}
progress.enough: You have shared enough to finish. More answers make the suggestions more reliable.

notice.paused: Saved. You can continue here later.
notice.completed: Finished. If you like, you can now ask for suggestions for your strengths.
notice.reading: Your answers are being read. The suggestions will appear here as soon as they are ready.

done.title: Your strengths interview is finished
done.text: {count, plural, one {One answer} other {# answers}} from this conversation.
done.askText: An AI on a Made2Found computer – not at an outside service – reads your answers and assigns strength themes to them. Each suggestion names the passage from your answer it rests on. The counter-questions are not analysed. Anything that cannot be backed up is not suggested.
done.unavailable: The analysis is not available right now. Your answers stay saved – you can ask for suggestions later. You can always record your own sentences under your strengths.
done.failed: Reading did not work. You can try again.
done.noneFound: No strength could be backed up well enough from this conversation. That says nothing about you – only that the answers do not describe enough behavior for it. You can do another interview or record something yourself.
done.allDecided: You have decided on all suggestions from this conversation.

proposals.title: Suggestions from your answers
proposals.text: None of this applies until you accept it. You can rewrite label and statement first.
proposals.levelNote: How well supported – not how strong.

review.title: Your answers
review.text: What you shared in this conversation.

again.text: You can do another strengths interview – for example with other situations.

interview.answerHint: At least {min} characters. Describe a situation – what happened, what did you do?
interview.answerPlaceholder: Describe what happened and what you did …
interview.tooShort: Still too short – at least {min} characters.
interview.restored: There was a longer text in this browser than the saved one. It is shown now.
interview.saveStateFailed: Not saved – the text is still in this browser
interview.followUpHint: These follow-up questions belong to the same answer – just keep writing.

took_charge.title: Tell me about a situation where you took responsibility although it was not clear at first who was in charge.
took_charge.hint: Work or private. It does not have to be big – what matters is what you did.

followUps.whatYouDidFirst: What was the first concrete thing you did?
followUps.whatWouldHaveHappened: What would have happened if you had not taken it on?
followUps.whatItCost: Was that easy for you, or did it cost energy? How did you notice?

hard_won.title: Tell me about something difficult that you managed in the end.
hard_won.hint: Work or private. Even if it only partly worked out.

followUps.whenItStalled: What did you do when things stalled?
followUps.whatItCost: What cost you the most energy, and what gave you energy?

solved_problem.title: Tell me about a problem you solved.
solved_problem.hint: A concrete problem with a before and an after – work or private.

followUps.howYouApproached: How did you go about understanding the problem?
followUps.whatWasYours: What of it was yours – and what was others'?
followUps.whatDidNotWork: What did you try first that did not work?

initiated.title: Tell me about something you got started without anyone asking you to.
initiated.hint: A project, a change, an initiative, a meeting – at work or in private life.

followUps.whoYouBroughtIn: Who did you win over for it – and how?

new_ground.title: Tell me about a situation where you had to get up to speed quickly on something new.
new_ground.hint: A new topic, a new role, a new environment – work or private.

followUps.howYouLearned: How did you concretely go about learning it?
followUps.whatYouDidDifferently: What did you do differently from others?
followUps.whatYouStillLacked: What were you still missing in the end, and how did you deal with it?

resistance.title: Tell me about a situation where you stood up for something or raised a topic although you expected resistance or conflict.
resistance.hint: An opinion, a decision, an uncomfortable topic – work or private.

followUps.howYouWentAboutIt: How exactly did you go about it?
followUps.whatItCost: What did it cost you – and would you do it again?

others_come.title: What do others repeatedly come to you for help with? Tell me about the most recent concrete case.
others_come.hint: The outside view. When several people ask you for the same thing, it shows something that is easy to overlook in yourself.

followUps.lastExample: What exactly was it about last time?
followUps.whatYouActuallyDo: What do you actually do that helps others?

decide_unclear.title: Tell me about a decision you had to make without all the information and under time pressure.
decide_unclear.hint: Work or private. This is about the situation, not whether the decision was right.

followUps.whatYouKnew: What did you know, and what not? What did you rely on?
followUps.howYouDecided: How did you get to the decision – whom did you talk to, what did you weigh?
followUps.whatYouWouldChange: What would you do differently today?

built_new.title: Tell me about something you designed or built anew – something that did not exist in that form before.
built_new.hint: A product, a process, an offer, an event – work or private.

followUps.whereTheIdeaCame: Where did the idea come from, and how did it grow?
followUps.howYouTestedIt: How did you find out whether it worked?
followUps.whatYouLeftToOthers: What did you leave to others, and why?

won_over.title: Tell me about a situation where you won someone over who initially did not want to.
won_over.hint: A customer, a colleague, an investor, a friend – work or private.

followUps.whatYouSaid: What did you say or do to open the conversation?
followUps.whatChangedTheirMind: What tipped it so the person went along?
followUps.whatYouWouldDoDifferently: What would you do differently next time?

helped_grow.title: Tell me about a moment when you helped someone get better or move forward.
helped_grow.hint: A colleague, a team member, a friend – work or private.

followUps.whatYouDid: What did you concretely do or say?
followUps.whatChangedForThem: What changed for that person afterwards?
followUps.whatItGaveYou: What did it give you – or cost you?

connected_people.title: Tell me about a situation where you connected people who did not know each other or did not work together before.
connected_people.hint: Two people or a whole group – work or private.

followUps.whyThosePeople: Why those people, and how did you notice they fit?

avoid_task.title: What kind of task do you put off the longest?
avoid_task.hint: It is about the kind of task, not a specific project. Honest, not polite.

hand_off.title: What do you gladly hand off, even though you could do it?
hand_off.hint: Tasks where you are happy when somebody else takes them on.

others_better.title: When did you notice that others do something better than you – and how did you notice?
others_better.hint: A concrete occasion where you saw: someone else does this better.

keep_going.name: Seeing it through
keep_going.shows: You keep going when it gets tough and nothing moves for a long time.
keep_going.helps: Helps in the long middle between idea and result.
keep_going.prompt: Where in our venture do we need someone who keeps going right now – and who of us already does?

reliable.name: Being dependable
reliable.shows: You keep your commitments; others do not have to chase you.
reliable.helps: Helps build trust with customers, partners and team.
reliable.prompt: What do we rely on each other for – and where is that not yet clear?

build_structure.name: Creating structure
build_structure.shows: You bring order to chaos: processes, responsibilities, clear next steps.
build_structure.prompt: Who of us brings structure when things get messy?

move_fast.name: Moving fast
move_fast.shows: You act quickly and do not wait for perfection.
move_fast.helps: Helps in early phases and under time pressure.
move_fast.prompt: When do we want to be fast, and when careful?

thorough.name: Working thoroughly
thorough.shows: You pay attention to detail and quality before something goes out.
thorough.helps: Helps with anything that is hard to fix later.
thorough.prompt: Which things must be especially clean for us – and who checks them?

take_ownership.name: Taking ownership
take_ownership.shows: You step in when nobody is responsible.
take_ownership.helps: Helps where roles are not yet settled.
take_ownership.prompt: Where does someone among us take responsibility without it being agreed?

hold_focus.name: Holding focus
hold_focus.shows: You set priorities and say no when something distracts.
hold_focus.prompt: Who of us reminds us of what matters most, and how do we say no?

convince.name: Convincing
convince.shows: You win others over with arguments and examples.
convince.helps: Helps in sales, fundraising and recruiting.
convince.prompt: Who of us leads which conversations where we need to win others over?

speak_plainly.name: Speaking plainly
speak_plainly.shows: You say uncomfortable things, even against resistance.
speak_plainly.helps: Helps when a team needs honest feedback.
speak_plainly.prompt: How do we want to tell each other uncomfortable things?

inspire.name: Inspiring
inspire.shows: You make a goal tangible and appealing to others.
inspire.helps: Helps with vision and building a team.
inspire.prompt: Who tells our story in a way that makes others want to join?

negotiate.name: Negotiating
negotiate.shows: You find solutions between different interests.
negotiate.helps: Helps with contracts, partnerships and terms.
negotiate.prompt: Who of us negotiates, and what is our bottom line?

make_visible.name: Making things visible
make_visible.shows: You bring ideas and results to the outside: presence, story, reach.
make_visible.helps: Helps with brand, visibility and sales.
make_visible.prompt: Who of us shows up externally, and who would rather not?

kick_off.name: Kicking things off
kick_off.shows: You start without anyone asking you to.
kick_off.prompt: Who of us kicks things off – and who slows them down when it gets too much?

decide.name: Deciding
decide.shows: You make decisions even with incomplete information.
decide.prompt: How do we decide when we disagree – and who gets the last word?

empathize.name: Empathizing
empathize.shows: You notice how others are doing and respond to it.
empathize.helps: Helps in customer conversations and team climate.
empathize.prompt: Who of us notices first when someone on the team is under pressure?

build_trust.name: Building trust
build_trust.shows: You are experienced as open and predictable.
build_trust.prompt: Whom do outsiders trust first among us – and why?

connect.name: Connecting
connect.shows: You bring the right people together.
connect.helps: Helps with network, partners and introductions.
connect.prompt: Who of us knows people who could help us, and how do we use that?

develop_others.name: Developing others
develop_others.helps: Helps with building and keeping talent.
develop_others.prompt: Who develops others among us – and who needs support right now?

resolve_conflict.name: Resolving conflict
resolve_conflict.shows: You raise tensions and find a way through.
resolve_conflict.helps: Helps when a team is under pressure.
resolve_conflict.prompt: How do we handle tension – and who raises it first?

build_cohesion.name: Building cohesion
build_cohesion.shows: You make a group feel like a team.
build_cohesion.prompt: What holds us together when things get difficult?

listen.name: Listening
listen.shows: You take it in before you answer.
listen.prompt: Who of us listens while others are still finding what they want to say?

spot_patterns.name: Spotting patterns
spot_patterns.shows: You see connections and repetition early.
spot_patterns.helps: Helps with markets, data and customer behaviour.
spot_patterns.prompt: Who of us sees patterns others do not see yet?

learn_fast.name: Learning fast
learn_fast.shows: You get up to speed quickly on new things.
learn_fast.helps: Helps when roles and topics change.
learn_fast.prompt: Who of us takes on new things when nobody has experience?

generate_ideas.name: Generating ideas
generate_ideas.shows: You come up with new paths and combinations.
generate_ideas.helps: Helps with product and business model.
generate_ideas.prompt: Where do new ideas come from among us – and who checks them?

envision_future.name: Envisioning the future
envision_future.shows: You think in scenarios and longer lines.
envision_future.prompt: Who of us thinks in three years, who in three weeks – and how do we connect both?

break_down.name: Breaking problems down
break_down.shows: You split complexity into clear parts.
break_down.prompt: Who of us breaks a big problem apart when we are stuck?

spot_opportunities.name: Spotting opportunities
spot_opportunities.shows: You see possibilities where others do not.
spot_opportunities.helps: Helps with market access and changes of direction.
spot_opportunities.prompt: What opportunity do we see – and who of us would be most likely to seize it?

experiment.name: Experimenting
experiment.shows: You test assumptions quickly and cheaply.
experiment.helps: Helps before much money and time is spent.
experiment.prompt: Which assumption could we test this week – and who tests it?

report.title: Your strengths in the founding day-to-day
report.text: These are themes that showed up in your own examples and that you accepted. They stand side by side as equals: no ranking, no number, no type.
report.levelNote: “Clearly shows” means: in at least three of your situations. “Shows”: in two. “Hint”: in one. That says how well it is supported – not how strong it is.
report.domainEmpty: Nothing has shown up here in your examples yet – that is fine, and a hint about who could complement you.

needs.title: Where you need support
needs.text: In your own words. This is not a weakness, but a hint about who could complement you.
needs.avoid_task: What you put off the longest

other.title: Other statements from you
other.text: Strengths you formulated yourself or accepted earlier.

report.emptyTitle: Your strengths picture comes from the strengths interview
report.emptyText: You have not accepted any strength themes yet. In the interview you tell about ten situations; suggestions arise from that, and you confirm them.

levelNoteShort: How well supported – not how strong.
